targets.authors: Hyland, P., McGinty, G., Karatzias, T., Murphy, J., Vallières, F., & McHugh Power, J.
targets.title: Can the REBT theory explain loneliness? Theoretical and clinical applications.
targets.evidence_quote: The current study replicates the analyses conducted by Hyland et al. (2019) using samples that (a) are larger, affording greater statistical power; (b) represent a more diverse collection of nations and continents; and (c) are either nationally representative or at least gender balanced.
targets.outcome_quote: In sum, then, the Hyland et al. findings were replicated with the larger and more diverse sample, indicating that their efficacy is not restricted to the undergraduate sample from the United Kingdom and Ireland on which they were originally tested.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall replication verdict governs both models. The discussion notes one differing pathway, but gives an overall successful verdict and repeats it in the conclusion. Reliability limitations do not negate that verdict.

reasoning: New multinational sample re-tests one published paper. Hyland 2014 supplies the measure and is not a target; intervention studies and other loneliness correlations provide background. Authors state an overall successful replication.
